lab_title: AR Exploration of DNA Structure and Semiconservative Replication
top_level_objectives: Visualize the 3D double-helix structure of DNA, including antiparallel sugar–phosphate backbones and inward-projecting base pairs.
Identify DNA components (5' and 3' ends, sugar–phosphate backbone, and bases A, T, G, C) and apply complementary base-pairing rules.
Explain semiconservative DNA replication by mapping parental versus newly synthesized strands in daughter molecules.
Connect the antiparallel geometry to replication-direction constraints (polymerase synthesizes 5'→3'), distinguishing leading vs. lagging synthesis.
Describe the roles of helicase, single-strand binding proteins, DNA polymerase, Okazaki fragments, and DNA ligase at the replication fork.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 1 — The Double Helix as a 3D Object
scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the DNA molecule in three dimensions and establish spatial intuition for the double helix axis.
key_visuals: A rotating 3D double helix centered in view
Clear highlighting of the two strands as they spiral around a shared central axis
A labeled direction cue indicating one strand’s 5' and the other strand’s 3' (antiparallel orientation preview)
student_actions: Rotate/tilt the DNA model to inspect how the two strands wrap around a common axis.
Point out which parts form the backbone versus the inner base region (using the on-screen prompts).

scenes.scene_name: Scene 2 — Components and Complementary Base Pairing
scenes.brief_purpose: Help students identify nucleotides and apply base-pairing rules in the 3D context.
key_visuals: Backbone highlighted (sugar–phosphate) along the outer spiral
Four base types labeled (A, T, G, C) projecting toward the interior
Animated pairing between bases across the helix showing hydrogen-bond counts (A–T: two, G–C: three)
student_actions: Select and label A, T, G, and C on the model.
Verify base pairing by checking that A pairs with T and G pairs with C, noting the corresponding hydrogen-bond number.

scenes.brief_purpose: Make the 5' and 3' ends physically meaningful and show how antiparallel orientation arises from the backbone.
key_visuals: End markers at both termini of each strand labeled 5' and 3'
Directional arrows placed along each backbone to show one strand runs 5'→3' while the complementary runs 3'→5'
A visual “track” overlay following one strand and then the opposite direction on the other strand
student_actions: Trace the backbone direction on each strand using the arrows provided.
Answer a prompt identifying which strand direction matches 5'→3' and which matches 3'→5' (based on the model’s labeled ends).

scenes.scene_name: Scene 4 — Replication Fork: Unwinding and Stabilizing Single Strands
scenes.brief_purpose: Connect DNA structure to replication initiation by showing what helicase and single-strand binding proteins do at the replication fork.
key_visuals: A replication-fork region shown as the DNA unwinds at a central “fork” point
Helicase activity indicated by separation of the two strands
Exposed single strands stabilized with a protective “coating” highlight symbolizing single-strand binding proteins
student_actions: Observe the double helix open into two templates and identify which region is the fork.
Describe (in a guided response) how single strands are prevented from re-annealing as replication begins.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 5 — DNA Polymerase and Asymmetry: Leading vs. Lagging
scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate why antiparallel structure forces different synthesis modes and how polymerase directionality (5'→3') shapes them.
key_visuals: DNA polymerase shown as an elongating enzyme moving along a template
A leading-strand synthesis path that extends continuously in the correct 5'→3' direction
A lagging-strand synthesis path where new segments start and extend discontinuously
Visual callouts marking 5' and 3' at template and growing strands to emphasize directionality
student_actions: Determine which daughter strand is leading and which is lagging based on continuous vs. discontinuous synthesis.
Explain how polymerase’s 5'→3' requirement forces the lagging strand to synthesize in segments.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 6 — Okazaki Fragments and Joining by DNA Ligase; Semiconservative Outcome
scenes.brief_purpose: Conclude by tying together fragments, ligation, and the semiconservative nature of replication.
key_visuals: Lagging strand showing multiple Okazaki fragments labeled sequentially
DNA ligase bridging fragment junctions and highlighting successful joining
Final “two daughter DNA” view where each is half parental (template-derived) and half new (synthesized)
student_actions: Identify Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand and indicate where ligase acts.
Confirm the semiconservative outcome by selecting one daughter molecule and tracing which strand is parental versus newly made.
